title: Choose the visual world for the NVD Watch scorecard
question: The roll assigned the EnergyGuide Label. Keep it, take the pick, adopt a declined challenger, take the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: EnergyGuide Label
options.lineage: FTC EnergyGuide appliance label, 1980 to today
options.thesis: The page is a mandated disclosure label for the NVD: one yearly-cost number, one comparative range bar, small print that defines every term.
options.viewport: Full-bleed yellow. Top strip in label small print: 'NVD Watch · U.S. Government vulnerability warning system · week ending Nov 7, 2026.' Below a heavy rule, the label's big number at poster scale: '22.6%' with 'of new CVEs carry scanner-matchable product data (CPE)' set condensed beside it. Below the next rule, the range bar: pointer at 22.6% on a bar whose ends read 'Not Scheduled 0%' and 'KEV-listed 94%'. A boxed 'Estimated yearly cost of the fix: $270K–$510K' sits right, with the OIG's $400K offset ticked on its own range bar. The primary action, 'Copy citation', is a black-filled label button with the yellow text; 'Download the brief (PDF)' beside it in outline. Section 2 begins below as the next labeled panel.
options.risk: Yellow at page scale can read as caution tape or kitsch if the ink is not kept to black and the rules to the label's exact weights. No dark mode: the label has one colour.

raised.raise: Definition beside every number: no figure appears without its one-line definition and source in the small-print voice, the way the shelf keeps recipe and risk beside each cup.
One ruled field grid for every metric: name, value, definition, source, in the same order on every panel, like the end-label grid ruling every box.
One ink only: black on yellow, hierarchy by weight, size, and rule thickness, never by a second colour.
Active state inverts: the selected control or pointer fills solid black, inactive ones sit as outlines, so state is unmistakable without colour.
Every panel and metric is addressable by URL, so a staffer can cite one figure with one link.
Provenance prints itself: 'Pulled 2026-11-07 19:21 UTC · 17,729 records · NVD API 2.0, CISA KEV, FIRST EPSS' set as text under the big number, never as a badge.

options.label: GAO Highlights Page
options.lineage: GAO report 'Highlights' page: Why GAO Did This Study, What GAO Found, What GAO Recommends
options.thesis: The scorecard as the one page staffers already read first: a blue identity band, a plain-serif 'What we found', and recommendations addressed to agencies by name.
options.viewport: Navy band across the top with the report-style title and date. Left column 'Why this matters' in a few lines; right column 'What we found' with the 22.6% figure as the first finding in bold serif, followed by the KEV gate and the cost. 'What we recommend' lists NIST, CISA, Congress with one line each. Citation and brief download sit in the band.
options.risk: This is where most runs for a policy audience land: a blue-banded report page. Familiar and effective, and hard to tell from a hundred agency sites.

options.label: Kiln Shelf Glaze Runs
options.lineage: glaze test tiles on a kiln shelf
options.thesis: CVEs as glaze runs that flow, stall, and pool on the shelf; pooled ones are the Not Scheduled stock.
options.viewport: A shelf row of cups, each a CVE tier, glaze running to the foot at the rate CPE arrives.
options.case: Policy staff do not identify with ceramics, and 'pooled glaze' hides the figure a staffer needs to quote.
options.kept: Recipe and risk beside every sample: definition beside every number.
options.risk: Beautiful and illegible to the reader who matters.

options.label: Sneaker Archive Wall
options.lineage: stacked sneaker boxes indexed by end labels
options.thesis: Each metric a box end label; pull a box to open its definition and data.
options.viewport: A wall of stacked boxes, the headline figure printed on the biggest end label.
options.case: No overlap with the audience's world; the stack metaphor slows a two-minute read.
options.kept: The end-label grid ruling every card: one field grid for every metric.
options.risk: Reads as a product page for shoes.

options.label: Photocopied Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: The scorecard as a folded insert: panels unfold in order, one ink weight, figures hand-numbered down the spine.
options.viewport: A folded panel with the week's figure crosshatched large; the tracklist is the four sections.
options.case: Lo-fi hand-drawn material undercuts a page whose whole claim is traceable evidence.
options.kept: One ink only; hierarchy without a second colour.
options.risk: Charming, and it reads as a zine, not a disclosure.

options.label: Itasha Vinyl Wrap
options.lineage: character-illustration car wraps with sponsor strips
options.thesis: The headline figure scaled to break across panel seams, recommendations as a sponsor strip along the sill.
options.viewport: A number so large it breaks across two panels, with a logo strip of stakeholders below.
options.case: Nothing in it belongs to a congressional or NIST reader; the seam device fights legibility.
options.kept: Active lifts to full gloss, inactive sits matte: an unmistakable active state.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Each section a one-bit card linked by painted buttons; every card addressable, back retraces the trail.
options.viewport: A fixed card with the week's figure in pixel type and four painted buttons to the sections.
options.case: Nostalgia for Mac users, not for policy staff; one-bit dither cannot carry a range bar or a chart cleanly.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The scorecard as a scrolling transcript: figures print themselves line by line in one monospaced face.
options.viewport: An 80-column transcript printing this week's coverage figures with a blinking cursor.
options.case: The cyber default this audience has seen on every vendor deck; a transcript hides the one number a staffer came for.
options.kept: System states print themselves as text: provenance printed, not badged.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A policy data dashboard: white ground, navy accent, four KPI tiles, a line chart, sticky section nav, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A headline, four stat tiles (coverage, KEV lag, cost, capacity), a chart, and a recommendations list below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every vulnerability-intelligence dashboard by design.
